x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text: D11, D20, and D49 schools are all closed today for Veterans Day. City offices closed too. This morning: Memorial Park ceremony at 11 AM. Free admission at the WWII Aviation Museum today. USAFA open to visitors. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text: COS families: Memorial Park ceremony at 11 AM, WWII Aviation Museum free all day, USAFA open to visitors. It's a good day to show kids what this city's military community looks like. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Happy Veterans Day, COS. 🇺🇸

D11, D20, and D49 schools are all closed today — and so are most City of Colorado Springs offices and El Paso County government buildings.

If your family has a free Wednesday on its hands, there's genuinely a lot to do. The WWII Aviation Museum at the Colorado Springs Airport is offering free admission today in honor of Veterans Day. The U.S. Air Force Academy is open to visitors. And this morning at 11 AM, there's a Veterans Day ceremony at Memorial Park — a simple, meaningful event worth attending if you have kids old enough to understand what it means.

Today is also just a good day to slow down and talk. Colorado Springs is one of the most military-connected cities in the country. For many families here, Veterans Day isn't an abstract holiday — it's personal.

What's your family doing today to mark Veterans Day?

stories.title: CPSC Recalls: 4 Children's Products Flagged in Early November

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text: 4 kids' products recalled this month: Magnetopia magnetic blocks, Arlopu slide playsets, Kikea nursing pillows, Baby Brezza sterilizers. Check cpsc.gov or call 1-800-638-2772. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text: If you have Magnetopia magnetic building blocks at home — these are recalled. Kids can swallow the magnets. Return or dispose immediately. Full list of November recalls at cpsc.gov. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Before the week gets away from you, check your home for these four products.

The Consumer Product Safety Commission posted four recalls in early November that every parent of young children should know about.

**Magnetopia Magnetic Building Cubes and Blocks** — recalled for magnet ingestion risk. Loose or swallowed magnets can attract through intestinal walls and cause serious internal injury. If you have these, stop use immediately.

**Arlopu Slide Playsets** — recalled because openings in the product can trap a child's torso, creating a head and neck entrapment hazard. The recall covers about 10,318 units.

**Kikea Store X-VESOLJE Nursing Pillows** — recalled for violating mandatory nursing pillow safety standards, posing a suffocation risk.

**Baby Brezza SuperFast Sterilizer Dryers** — recalled because the unit can overheat while operating, creating a burn hazard if the surface is handled.

For refunds or replacements, check cpsc.gov or call the CPSC hotline at 1-800-638-2772. All four recalls were posted on November 5, 2026.

Do you check the CPSC recall list regularly? It updates weekly — worth bookmarking.

stories.title: COS Holiday Season Launches This Week — Ice Rink, Character Strolls, More

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text: COS holiday season starts THIS WEEK: Acacia Park ice rink opens Thursday (kids 4 and under free). Holiday Character Stroll Friday 11 AM–1 PM (Santa, Grinch, Elsa, Anna). Anastasia the Musical opens Thu at ENT Center. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
The COS holiday season officially kicks off this week — and the schedule is packed.

**Thursday, November 13:** Acacia Park's outdoor ice rink opens for the season. Kids 4 and under skate free. It's one of the best free family activities downtown, and the first week is always festive. The ENT Center for the Arts at UCCS also opens Anastasia the Musical — Youth Edition on Thursday evening.

**Friday, November 14:** The Holiday Character Stroll runs 11 AM to 1 PM at Acacia Park, 115 E. Platte Ave. Families can get photos with Santa, the Grinch, Elsa, and Anna. No tickets needed — just show up.

**Every Tuesday through December 22:** Bass Pro Shops hosts story time with Santa and Mrs. Claus at 5 PM. Reservations are required and can be made up to 7 days in advance.

**November 27–29:** The Nutcracker at the Pikes Peak Center, presented by the Colorado Springs Philharmonic with the Colorado Springs Children's Chorale. Tickets start at $40.

The holiday season in COS really is something — this city goes all out. Which event is your family most excited for?

stories.title: AAP Flu Guidance for 2026–2027: Vaccinate Now, Doses Unchanged

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text: The AAP updated its flu guidance for 2026–2027. Doses are unchanged. Colorado's flu season peaks Jan–Feb — which means NOW is when to get kids vaccinated, not when everyone's already sick. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
The American Academy of Pediatrics just released its updated influenza prevention recommendations for the 2026–2027 season, and the main message is: if your child hasn't been vaccinated yet, don't wait.

The number of doses recommended for children remains unchanged from last season. For most children 9 and older who've had a flu vaccine before, that's one dose. For some younger children getting vaccinated for the first time, it may be two doses four weeks apart — your pediatrician can confirm.

The timing matters. Colorado's flu season typically peaks between January and February, which means kids vaccinated now will have full protection when it's needed most. Earlier this month, Colorado reported its first child flu death of the 2026–2027 season — a reminder that flu isn't just inconvenient, it can be serious.

If your family has already gotten vaccinated, you're ahead. If not, this week is a good week to call your pediatrician or stop by a pharmacy.

stories.title: Talking to COS Kids About Veterans Day: Age-by-Age Guide

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: COS is home to Fort Carson, the USAFA, Peterson, Schriever, and Cheyenne Mountain. A lot of COS kids know veterans personally. Here's an age-by-age guide for talking about today with kids ages 3–teen. #COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Colorado Springs is one of the most military-connected communities in the country. Fort Carson, the U.S. Air Force Academy, Peterson Space Force Base, Schriever Space Force Base, Cheyenne Mountain Space Force Station — all within the Pikes Peak region. Many COS kids have a parent, grandparent, aunt, or uncle who served or is currently serving.

That makes Veterans Day feel different here than it does in a lot of places. It's not abstract for a lot of our kids. So how do you talk about it in an age-appropriate way?

**Ages 3–5:** Keep it simple and concrete. "Veterans Day is a day we say thank you to the people who kept us safe." If you know a veteran personally, today is a great day to call them.

**Ages 6–10:** You can go a little deeper. Talk about the different branches of the military, what service means, and why we set aside a day to honor it. COS's military installations give kids here a real connection to these ideas.

**Ages 11 and older:** Teens can handle history and nuance. Talk about why Veterans Day is in November, what Armistice Day was, and what service has meant in your own family's story.

If you're out today, the Memorial Park ceremony at 11 AM is a meaningful place to bring kids of all ages. The WWII Aviation Museum is free today and excellent for school-age kids.

How does your family mark Veterans Day?
